> In Ashadha Prataparudra sits in the Lord's house;
Advaita, smiling, speaks of Krishna.
> [p. 225]
> Standing, the Lord wets the string of his loincloth […];
"Give my body to the fire […], my life" […].*
> Mahendra Bharati died [by] […] haritaki;*
three hundred yatis put fire in his mouth.
> Haridasa Thakura departed first,
on the bright fourteenth day of Phalguna.
> In Ashadha, as he was dancing at the chariot procession,
suddenly a brick struck his left foot.
> Advaita set out at dawn for the land of Gauda;
in private [the Lord] told him something particular there.
> In the waters of Narendra, with all his companions,
Chaitanya sported in the water in many ways.
> On the sixth day the pain in his foot was great;
on that account he at last lay down in the Tota.
> To Pandita Gosani he told everything:
"Tomorrow, at the tenth danda of the night, I shall surely go."
> From somewhere came divine garlands of many colours;
how many vidyadharas dance on the royal road!
> "Bring the chariot, bring the chariot!" the gods call out;
the Lord mounted the chariot with the Garuda banner.
> The illusory body remained lying there;
Chaitanya went to Vaikuntha, leaving Jambudvipa.
> Many servants died of snakebite;
there were meteors, thunderbolts, earthquakes.
> Nityananda and Advaita Acharya Gosani heard;
Vishnupriya and Shachi Thakurani fainted.
> Sri Ramadasa [came] with all the companions;
Nityananda consoled [them], giving them comfort.
> Purushottama and the other companions of Advaita,
hearing of Chaitanya's departure, were struck dumb.
> In separation from Chaitanya, Nityananda constantly
listens to [the tale of] the lila of Chaitanya's departure.
> Nityananda, consoling all the companions,
dances in the bliss of Chaitanya, in the wealth of kirtana:
> "If I bear the name Nityananda Svarupa,
if I do not make Vaishnavas of all, down to the chandala, [—]
> I will make no distinction of caste for chandala or yavana;
giving prema-bhakti to all, I will make them dance in kirtana."
> Sri Ramadasa holds all power:
he will reveal the fifty-six crores of the Yadu line.
> "I will make the wives of good families dance in the bliss of kirtana;
the blind, the deaf and the dull will dance at will.
> I will bring Chaitanya, I will make people accept that Chaitanya;
I will make the kingdoms of Gauda and Utkala blessed, blessed."
> Hearing this vow of Nityananda,
all the Vaishnavas raise the cry, "Glory, glory!"
> After some days Nityananda, wearing the shikha and the sacred thread,
wandered the earth in the guise of a great wrestler.
> The daughters of Suryadasa, Sri Vasu and Jahnava,*
he took in marriage, freely and merrily.
> From Vasu's womb appeared Gosani Virabhadra;
Jahnava's son is Ramabhadra, a great wrestler.*
> Murari Chaitanyadasa catches and brings a tiger;
he sleeps on a bed of snakes — all people know it.
> Sri Sundarananda Thakura, in the water,
catches a crocodile and brings it before everyone.
> Disputing with the Kazi, in the madness of prema,
Gangadasa stayed seven days in a pool of the Ganga.
> Great was the madness of prema of Kamalakara Pippalai:
he cut his own body, and yet he did not come to himself.
> Gadadhara Dasa disputed with the Kazi
and leapt into a pit of fire — seeing it, the people were afraid.
> Purushottama Dasa ate the poison of the mandara*
and digested the poison by the power of the bliss of prema.
> [p. 226]
> As Sanjaya Pandita danced in the mood of a child,
suddenly a snake came out of his mouth.
> In ecstasy Murari Gupta became Hanuman:
a tail came out of him, twelve cubits long.
> Purandara Pandita climbs to the top of a tree;
a sixteen-cubit tail hangs down to the foot of the tree.
> Parameshvara Dasa ate three measures* of earth;
Balarama Dasa burns [the dwellings?] of the yavanas.*
> Kaliya Krishnadasa binds and brings a crocodile;
seeing it, Sri Nityananda's delight increased.
> Sri Nityananda made his home at Khardaha,
where the line of the great kulina Yogeshvara lives.*
> Advaita-chandra's line dwells in Shantipur:
the sons and grandsons of Sita and Advaita appear.
> Sankirtana and temples will be in every kingdom:
[by this] weighty deed he removed the earth's burden.
> The treasure of Chaitanya's life is Lord Nityananda:
not for an instant did he see [him] in separation, as if he were blind.*
> Nityananda always stays at home;
Gauridasa Pandita gives him help.
> Gauridasa Pandita — the four brothers together —
with Nityananda merrily carry on the dhamali of rapture.
> Thousands upon thousands — so many servants of Advaita!
Their servants fill the world.
> The servants of Chaitanya are without limit;
the servants of Nityananda have great prosperity.
> All the servants who are with Nityananda-chandra
I could not tell in a thousand years.
> Each servant has a following of thousands upon thousands;
by Nityananda's grace they are like Krishna.
> In the Kali age the world became righteous;
all the heavy burden of the earth was removed.
> Nityananda said to Gauridasa Pandita:
"[…] Pandita, I remain on this earth."*
> In the month of Ashvina, at a conjunction, on the dark eighth lunar day,
Nityananda went to Vaikuntha, leaving the earth.
> On the day of Ekadashi it was like the dissolution of the world:
at the breath of Ananta the earth trembled.
> The mahantas who heard of Nityananda's departure,
seeing Virabhadra, were wholly comforted.
> Sita and Advaita were left with great grief in their hearts:
"Alas, Chaitanya, Nityananda Svarupa!"
> Acharya Gosani passed some more days;
"I shall leave the earth," he said of his own accord.
> On the bright thirteenth lunar day of the month of Pausha
Acharya Gosani departed to Vaikuntha.
> Svasti! Glory, glory to the Chaitanya-mangala,
the crest-jewel of avataras, in which all is revealed!
> Whoever sings of Chaitanya, or makes others sing of Chaitanya,
is Chaitanya's servant, and Chaitanya is his helper.
> To his sons, grandsons, great-grandsons and all the rest
Jayananda's blessing: the fulfilment of their wishes.
> Meditating on the two feet of Chaitanya and Gadadhara,
Jayananda joyfully sings the Uttara-khanda." The end.
notes: "রুধিআ মাএর মুখে ইটাল মারিঞা" — the sense is conjectural.
Hari-vasara — the Ekadashi day; the episode meant is the one in which the child Nimai demanded and ate the food prepared as an offering to Vishnu in the house of Jagadisha and Hiranya.
"চৈতন্যেতে গুরুতে মারিল পুথির বাড়ি" — the beginning of the line is unclear.
"ছালিয়াধরা" — the name (or nickname) is unidentified; the reading follows the OCR.
"পাটুআ" — jute (or jute leaves eaten as a vegetable); Sridhara is the poor trader with whom, according to the biographies, Nimai bargained in the market.
"সাপে মুক্ত করিল কুকুর গঙ্গাদাস" — the sense is unclear (taken as "শাপে মুক্ত," "freed from a curse").
"পণ্ডিত হএ বক," literally "panditas become herons," i.e. apparently they fall dumb or look foolish; the sense is conjectural.
A digvijayi, "conqueror of the quarters," is a wandering scholar who defeated all comers in debate.
I.e. Lakshmipriya, Chaitanya's first wife.
"বাপ মরিতে গয়া যাইতে" — the journey to Gaya for the funeral rite for his father; Rajagiri (Rajgir) — hills near Gaya.
The connection of the line with its context is unclear: Madhavendra Puri was the guru of Ishvara Puri.
"বুড়ি," an old woman; the episode is known only from Jayananda.
"বায়ু," "wind," i.e. a disorder of the wind (vata) in the body — an illness taken for madness.
"বিষ্ণুখট্টা," the seat (couch) of Vishnu, i.e. the throne of the deity.
"দাসী-পুত্র," "son of a maidservant"; who is meant is unclear (perhaps Murari himself, so naming himself in humility).
The second line of this couplet is missing in the OCR.
"ধুবালিআ সিন্ধালিআ" — apparently nicknames of Jagai and Madhai; the reading follows the OCR.
The OCR has "নিশ্বলিয়া," "লিমলিয়া"; according to the biographies, the Kazi's house stood at Simulia (সিমুলিয়া) near Navadvipa.
"সাত-প্রহরিয়া ভাব," the ecstasy of "seven watches," i.e. the great manifestation (mahaprakasha) that lasted twenty-one hours.
"ভক্ত করি সভার বহিল সাজি ধুতি" — the sense is unclear.
"দুখী দাসী" may also be taken as a name: Duhkhi was a maidservant in Srivasa's house.
Whom the king's man seized is not clear from the text.
"আগম পুথি," the books of the agamas (tantras); perhaps Nityananda's abandonment of earlier rites is meant. The first line of the couplet is incomplete.
"উদ্‌গ্রাহ" — an argument or rejoinder in learned debate; cf. above, the section on language, word 9.
"ত্রিপাদ" — apparently the form of Trivikrama, who covered the worlds in three strides. The Kshetra is Puri.
"রদ্ক অনুগ্রহ মাত্র প্রদ্যুম্ন কানাঞি" — the line is corrupt (perhaps it concerns Pradyumna Mishra or Kanu).
Angada — one of the monkey leaders in the Ramayana.
"জম্বীর" — the lime (citron) tree.
Dana-khanda — songs about Krishna exacting "toll" from the gopis.
Dabir Khas and Sakar Malik — the court titles of Rupa and Sanatana in the service of the sultan of Gauda.
"দ্বার ছাড়ি" — perhaps Haridvar; the sense is conjectural.
Trimalla-raya — the deity on the Venkata hill (Tirumala, Venkateshvara); the second half of the line is unclear.
"কুড়িয়া গরুড়মিশ্র" — the reading follows the OCR; the person is unidentified.
Mahrat, Sorai, Viranchi — readings follow the OCR; the places are unidentified.
"হেমসেতু" — the sense is unclear (perhaps "as far as the Setu," i.e. the southern tip of India).

Vasu's note. According to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, [Chaitanya] lived twenty-four years as a householder and twenty-four years as a sannyasi in Nilachala. But according to Jayananda, Gauranga took sannyasa in his twentieth year, thus: "Fourth, the Sannyasa-khanda — listen with one mind — how [he took] sannyasa and the name Sri Krishna-Chaitanya. Young in years was Gaurachandra, twenty years old; a man of great renunciation, his body pure gold."
The couplet is corrupt ("দাঁড়াএ প্রভুর তিতে কৌপীনের ডোর। অগ্নি দেহ অন্য কনাএ কুঞ্জ প্রাণ মোর"); the rendering is a guess.
"হরিতকী কাষ্ঠে" — the sense is unclear; Mahendra Bharati is unidentified.
The OCR has "শ্রীবস্থ জানকী"; below it has "জাহ্নবীনন্দন," so we read "Jahnava." These are Vasudha and Jahnava, Nityananda's wives.
"জাহ্নবীনন্দন রামভদ্র মহামল্ল" — so in the text; cf. what is known of Ramachandra, Jahnava's adopted son.
"মণ্ডর বিষ" — reading and sense unclear.
"আড়ি" — a measure of grain.
"জবনের সাড়ি" — the sense is unclear.
I.e. the line to which Suryadasa, Nityananda's father-in-law, belonged.
The line is unclear; perhaps "like a blind man [without his guide]."
"নিষ্কপটে পণ্ডিত আমি আছি এই মহী" — the sense is unclear.

verses_en.text:
The last scene (translated from the Chaitanya-mangal of Jayananda, p. 150):*
When dancing at the Bijaya of the Car festival in the month of Asharh, His left toe was suddenly pierced by a brick [lying on the road]. When Adwaita left for Bengal, the Master secretly told him [of His coming disappearance]. With all His followers He sported in the water of the Narendra tank [for the last time]. On the sixth day of the moon, the pain in His toe grew severer, and He was forced to take to His bed in the garden. Here He told the Pandit Goswami that He would leave the earth next night at 10 o clock. Celestial garlands of many-coloured flowers were thrown on Him from the unseen. Celestial singers (vidyadhar) began to dance on the highway. The gods began to cry out, "Bring the heavenly chariot!" The Master mounted into Vishnu's car with the figure of Garuda on its spire. His material body lay behind on the earth, while He went to Vaikuntha (Vishnu's heaven). Many of His servants killed themselves by serpent-bite. Meteors and thunderbolts fell on the earth. At the news Nityananda and Adwaita Acharya, Vishnupriya and Shachi swooned away. Purushottam and other servitors of the Master grew speechless at His departure.
notes: Sarkar translates from the 1905 edition of the Chaitanya-mangala (Bangiya Sahitya Parishat, ed. N. Vasu and K. Nath). The same episode from Vasu's manuscript (folios 75–76) is translated in `02-vasu-1897.md` (the section on Mahaprabhu's disappearance, notes 67–68). Agreements: the wound from a brick to the left foot while dancing at the car festival; the secret word to Advaita before his departure for Gauda; the water-play in the Narendra lake; the pain growing worse on the sixth day; the Lord taking to his bed at Tota (Sarkar's "garden" is a literal rendering of tota); the words to the Pandita Gosani (probably Gadadhara) that he would depart the next night; the garlands, the dancing vidyadharas, the gods' cry "Bring the chariot!", the chariot with the Garuda banner (Sarkar: "figure … on its spire"); the body left on earth; the servants' death by snake-bite; the falling meteors and thunderbolts. Differences: Vasu's extract opens with two couplets absent in Sarkar (Chaitanya at Tota announces his departure and asks for the chariot to be sent on the bright seventh lunar day of Ashadha), and it ends with the portents, whereas Sarkar continues (the swoons of Nityananda, Advaita, Vishnupriya and Shachi, Purushottama's speechlessness, Nityananda's vow) beyond Vasu's quotation; Vasu's portents also include an earthquake, which Sarkar lacks; "the tenth danda of the night" (about four hours after sunset) is rendered by Sarkar as "10 o clock"; where Vasu has the "illusory body", Sarkar has the "material body"; the obscure word before "car procession" (Vasu, note 67) is passed over by Sarkar, who keeps only "Bijaya" (going forth, procession). Sarkar translates in free prose and abridges in places. Sarkar's dating (the poem c. 1568) is later than Vasu's (shortly after 1480 Shaka, i.e. c. 1558); the birth year c. 1511 agrees with Vasu's conclusions (`02-vasu-1897.md`, note 24).

jayananda-cm.ref: Уттара-кханда: краткое жизнеописание (Н. Васу 1897); Дж. Саркар 1922; цит. «После ухода Чайтаньи»
jayananda-cm.title: После ухода: скорбь спутников и обет Нитьянанды
jayananda-cm.summary: Нитьянанда и Адвайта узнают об уходе, Вишнуприя и Шачи лишаются чувств; Рамадас и спутники Адвайты онемели; Нитьянанда утешает всех и даёт обет: сделает вайшнавами всех, вплоть до чандалов и яванов, не различая каст, и даст всем прему-бхакти; «Кто пришёл — Адвайта, тот и есть Чайтанья». Вайшнавы восклицают: «Слава!»

verses.text:
Нитьянанда и Адвайта Ачарья Госани услышали;
Вишнуприя и Шачи-тхакурани лишились чувств.
> Шри Рамадас со всеми спутниками [пришёл];
Нитьянанда утешил [их], ободрив.
> Пурушоттама и другие спутники Адвайты,
услышав об уходе Чайтаньи, онемели.
> В разлуке с Чайтаньей Нитьянанда непрестанно
слушает [повествование] об игре ухода Чайтаньи.
> Нитьянанда, утешив всех спутников,
пляшет в блаженстве Чайтаньи, в богатстве киртана:
> «Если я ношу имя Нитьянанда Сварупа,
если не сделаю вайшнавами всех, вплоть до чандалов, [—]
> не буду различать каст ни у чандала, ни у явана;
дав всем прему-бхакти, заставлю их плясать в киртане».
> Шри Рамадас обладает всей силой:
он явит пятьдесят шесть крор рода Яду.
> «Заставлю плясать жён из добрых семей в блаженстве киртана;
слепые, глухие и тупые будут плясать вольно.
> Приведу Чайтанью, дам людям принять этого Чайтанью;
царства Гауды и Уткалы сделаю благословенными».
> Услышав этот обет Нитьянанды,
все вайшнавы восклицают: «Слава, слава!»

Нитьянанда утешил учеников и поклялся перед ними: «Мы сохраним Имя живым. Мы сделаем всех людей, вплоть до чандалов, вайшнавами. Мы не будем делать различия для [низких] каст вроде чандалов или мусульман, но всем дадим любовь и бхакти и всех заставим плясать [с нами] на киртане. Мы сделаем благословенными царства Бенгалии и Ориссы». Вайшнавы громкими возгласами одобрили его слова.
[= краткое жизнеописание Чайтаньи в конце поэмы, приведённое Н. Васу (1897).]*
notes: «Нитьянанда и Адвайта Ачарья Госани услышали; / Вишнуприя и Шачи-тхакурани лишились чувств».

verses.text: «Пришёл я — Адвайта; кто пришёл, тот и есть Чайтанья;

jayananda-cm.from: > Нитьянанда и Адвайта Ачарья Госани усл

verses_en.text:
"First the Lord's birth and deeds are revealed:
in the month of Phalguna Rahu swallowed the moon whole.
> Nimai, Gauranga, and first of all Vishvambhara by name —
these three names are an abode of blessing for the world.
> Seeing on his lotus feet the marks of banner, thunderbolt and goad,
Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra were very happy at heart.
> At six months, as he slept on a bedstead,
a snake held its hood over his head — all the people saw it.
> On the pretext of crying, how much magic he worked!
All the people joyfully said, "Hari, Hari!"
> Every day he played with the children in the middle of the courtyard;
all say: golden anklets ring on his feet.
> Thieves, greedy for wealth, carried him off to kill him;
leading the thieves astray, the Lord came back home.
> [p. 221]
> With the children on the bank of the Ganga, in a little house of sand,
clapping his hands, he revealed kirtana there.
> Striking his mother in the face with a brick,
he gave her tulasi buds, proclaiming bhakti.*
> Day and night Jagadisha in Hiranya's house —
on the day of Hari the Lord ate [their] offering.*
> A brahmana came and offered food to Krishna —
[the Lord,] touching it, ate his rice and curries.
> Sudarshana Pandita put chalk into his hands;
[…] he struck his teacher with a book.*
> When the time came for piercing his ears,
a garland fell from heaven onto the pot of Ganesha.
> Chhaliyadhara,* the king's messenger, was bitten by a snake;
making him say "Krishna," [the Lord] took away his pride.
> Stealing jute from Sridhara,*
he grew headstrong, heeding no one's word.
> From Burana came Sri Haridasa;
he freed the dog Gangadasa from a curse.*
> He fulfilled the desires of all the wives of good families;
soon his elder brother took sannyasa.
> At an auspicious moment the tonsure and the upanayana were performed;
Gauranga took on a form that charms women.
> Expounding the Kalapa, he became a teacher;
in explaining word and meaning, panditas [before him] are herons.*
> Gangadasa Pandita, well known in Navadvipa —
in his house he revealed all learning.
> Merely by discussing the Kalapa he knew everything;
disputing, he taught in Navadvipa.
> Mishra Purandara departed to Vaikuntha;
handsome Gauranga married Lakshmi.
> In every sutra he expounded devotion to Vishnu;
no one had the power to understand that exposition.
> Then the Lord defeated the conqueror of the quarters*
and at last destroyed all his bonds.
> Telling Gadadhara and Srinivasa in particular,
on the pretext of earning money he went to Vanga.
> The eastern land, Vanga, then became a tirtha;
by a snakebite mother Lakshmi* went to Vaikuntha.
> Returning from Vanga, marrying Vishnupriya,
he roams joyfully about the city of Nadia.
> When his father died,* going to Gaya, he saw Ishvara Puri;
staying on the Rajagiri hill, [he] showed him grace.
> With water that had washed the feet of brahmanas he removed the burden of sins;
the lord of munis, Madhavendra Puri, sees the six-armed form in the matha.*
> At Gayashira he offered pindas at Vishnu's footprint
and delivered all his ancestors one by one.
> In Gaya Gauranga's glory grew greatly:
by the touch of his feet a stone image was set free.
> An old brahmana woman gave him water that had washed [his] feet —
drinking the foot-water, the old woman vanished.*
> Returning from Gaya, in Srinivasa's house
he had kunda flowers gathered every evening.
> Then for some days he was seized by "wind";*
he revealed all the prema-bhakti there is.
> In Srinivasa's house, on Vishnu's throne,*
the Lord revealed himself in the sight of all.
> Nityananda Gosani left Varanasi;
hearing of Gauranga's glory, he came to Navadvipa.
> He showed the six-armed form to Nityananda Svarupa,
[who] stayed in the house of Nandana Acharya in Navadvipa.
> He showed the Boar form to Murari Gupta;
mounting his shoulders, he showed grace to the son of a maidservant.*
> In ecstasy Gaurachandra became the Haladhara;
Nityananda put plough and pestle into his hands.
> [p. 222]
> When the time of the shraddha of Srinivasa's father drew near […].*
> At mealtime the Lord's hair came loose;
becoming four-armed, he tied it up with two hands.
> Nityananda, on the pretext of the Vyasa-puja, broke his staff;
Gauranga, with a leap, falls into the water of the Ganga.
> He freed Jagai and Madhai from great sin,
the two robber brothers Dhubalia and Sindhalia.*
> Breaking the Kazi's house in the village of Simulia,*
in the "seven-watch" ecstasy* he was full of joy.
> In every house in Navadvipa, Hari-sankirtana;
the yavanas fled, leaving the village of Simulia.
> Shuklambara Brahmachari's bag of alms
[the Lord] snatched and ate from; the brahmana was dismayed.
> Dancing in sankirtana, he took on the mood of Rukmini;
he gave the breast to all the Vaishnavas.
> All the Vaishnavas see the Lord's various forms;
praising him, all received boons one by one.
> Haridasa received Gauranga's remnants;
[the Lord] drank water from Sridhara's broken iron pot.
> Taking all the companions, together with Nityananda,
he went to Advaita's house, in various delights.
> In Srinivasa's house the Lord dances in sankirtana,
offering everyone the wealth of Vaikuntha — prema.
> Srinivasa's dead son speaks of the truth of the soul;
the grief for his son went far away; [Srinivasa] remains in sankirtana.
> Great was Gauranga's favour to Srinivasa:
at Gauranga's words he forgot his grief for his son.
> […] carried baskets and dhotis for everyone;*
he punished Devananda Pandita.
> All the companions who were in various lands
then came to Navadvipa and gathered together.
> He mocked the great students with a shloka;
the people of Navadvipa could not recognise him.
> Performing bali, vaishvadeva, shraddha — the observances of a brahmana —
[he showed such] purity that Navadvipa marvelled.
> Chaitanya saw the land of his fathers, Jayapura;
he showed great mercy to the maidservant Duhkhi.*
> Through the mouth of Narayani, Srinivasa's niece,
making her say "Hari," he made her weep in the joy of prema.
> As he danced in kirtana, "wind" arose in the Lord;
an exorcist, tying the Lord's feet with a rope, held him.
> The king's man came, seized [someone] and takes him away;
the Lord makes him say "Hari" and weep.*
> In the son of Acharya Gosani, Sri Achyutananda,
Gaurachandra revealed himself — in his body.
> Haridasa Thakura receives the remnants from the Lord's plate,
and only Narayani eats the rest of the remnants.
> In renunciation he revealed the truth to all;
he consoled Vishnupriya with tales of itihasa.
> Leaving the happy household life in Navadvipa,
he revealed himself at Katwa on the bank of the Jahnavi.
> In sannyasa he took the name Sri Krishna-Chaitanya;
seeing him, the people of the world say, "Blessed, blessed!"
> Keshava Bharati, seeing and hearing of the four-armed [form], […];
Nityananda, turning back, threw away the books of the agamas.*
> Vakreshvara, having set out, turned back again;
[the Lord] stayed twelve days in Shantipur.
> Nityananda ran on ahead to Nilachala;
[the Lord] stayed in seclusion; no one could see him.
> Consoling Advaita, he went to Nilachala,
wandering from land to land, from forest to forest.
> Kashi Mishra's house, the Tota — a delightful place:
by Jagannatha's command he took up residence there.
> [p. 223]
> With Sarvabhauma there was a discussion of Vedanta;
hearing [his] arguments,* Sarvabhauma marvelled.
> He showed Sarvabhauma the six-armed form;
Vidya-vachaspati saw the three strides in the Kshetra.*
> Paramananda Puri Gosani met [him] at Setu-bandha;
[the Lord] showed great grace to Raya Ramananda.
> King Prataparudra saw the eight-armed [form];
[the Lord] placed his lotus feet on Vaninatha Pattanayaka.
> […] grace only to Pradyumna […]* —
in his lap Chaitanya Gosani fell asleep.
> Vishnu Puri, Damodara, Vishveshvara,
Govinda and Govindananda — ever with him.
> By Jagannatha's command, in special bliss,
setting out for Mathura, he entered the land of Gauda.
> He stayed in seclusion in the house of Vidya-vachaspati;
all the people, going round the town, saw him.
> With many companions, in special bliss,
he sent Nityananda Svarupa to the land of Gauda.
> On the way Sri Ramadasa is in the divine mood:
people see [him] thrice-bent with a flute and are afraid.
> With a basket of curds on his head, Gadadhara Dasa
in the middle of the road revealed the mood of Radha.
> Parameshvara Dasa entered the divine mood;
Purandara Pandita is drunk with the mood of Angada.*
> Uprooting a tree, he climbs onto the branches of a tree;
someone, rolling over, falls from the roof of a house.
> Raghunatha Vaidya Upadhyaya, the great-minded —
he became like [Nityananda] in Nityananda's mood.
> For three months [Nityananda] was beside himself, at his own will,
in Raghava Pandita's house in the village of Panihati.
> Sri Ramadasa, laughing in the mood of Krishna —
kadamba flowers blossomed on a lime tree.*
> Gadadhara Dasa makes everyone dance in his house;
the singer Madhava Ghosha sings the Dana-khanda.*
> Nityananda makes the Kazi say "Hari bol";
Murari Chaitanyadasa has a quarrel with Raghava.
> He stays submerged in the water for five or seven days;
a black snake bites him — blood flows from his body.
> At Saptagrama Nityananda, in a merchant's house,
dances day and night at a great festival.
> Gold, silver, diamonds, pearls, anklets,
a profusion of lovely painted silks.
> At Shantipur, in Advaita's house, Nityananda
roams at will with Achyutananda.
> At Navadvipa, in Hiranya's house, Nityananda —
a robber brahmana went at night to murder him.
> The night passed; the robber fled in fear:
in storm, rain and darkness he went blind.
> Showing great grace to the robber brahmana,
[Nityananda] sees him floating in tears of prema and thrills.
> In Nilachala the brahmanas and Gauranga remained;
the Lord entrusted the kingdom of Gauda to Nityananda.
> After some days, at the time of the Ratha-yatra, Nityananda
went to Nilachala with all the companions.
> [The Lord] undid the worldly bonds of the Dabir Khas;
to the two brothers he gave the names Rupa and Sanatana.*
> Gaurachandra set out again for Mathura;
Nityananda flooded Gauda with sankirtana.
> Gaurachandra went on pilgrimage to Varanasi
and duly put to shame a heretical sannyasi.
> He went to Prayaga and bathed [at] Veni-Madhava;
at Ayodhya, the Sarayu, the Gharghara, the place of sacrifice.
> Leaving Dvar,* the Lord went quickly
by many difficult roads to Mathura.
> [p. 224]
> He saw at Mathura Madanamohana,
the Kalindi, Kadamba-tala, Mount Govardhana.
> Keshi-ghat, Vamshi-vata he saw one by one;
Bhandira, Bahulavana he saw each.
> The birthplace, the Ranga-bhumi, Vishrama-ghat,
Govinda-raya, Bhratri-vata[?], the stone slab.
> By another road, in the land of Trimalla, on the Venkata mountain,
he saw Trimalla-raya, jewels streaming from his head.*
> The leper Garuda Mishra* he cured of his leprosy
and sent him with his wife to Nilachala.
> Mahrat, Sorai, Shiva-Kanchi, Vishnu-Kanchi;
passing through Vijayanagara he went to Viranchi.*
> Crossing the Mahanadi he went to Nilachala
and remained in Nilachala twenty-eight years.
> All people became righteous, the earth was blessed;
he made a flood of prema reaching to Hemasetu.*
> In the ocean of prema, with Nityananda at the helm,
the cargo of Kali's sins sank in the deep.
> Yama's abode became empty, [and] the torments of hell;
Yama went to Brahma to take counsel.
> Yama says: "Brahma, relieve me of my office:
Sri Chaitanya Thakura has delivered all the sinners.
> All the eighty-four pits of hell have become empty;
sixty thousand messengers sit idle at home.
> Some sinners Sri Jagannatha delivered,
some sinners were freed by the rice of mahaprasada;
> some sinners were freed by serving tulasi,
some sinners were freed by the Ganga and Varanasi;
> some sinners were freed by the shalagrama stone,
some, some sinners were freed by Hari-nama.
> Yama's abode has become empty; there are no more sinners."
Hearing Yama's words, Brahma laughs right there.
> With Indra and Shankara he set out himself;
all the gods together raise cries of victory.
> In Nilachala, at night, Chaitanya in the Tota ashrama
announced in due order that he would go to Vaikuntha:
> "Having agreed on the bright seventh lunar day of Ashadha,
send a chariot — I will go to the city of Vaikuntha."
> Nityananda came [to Nilachala] near the time of the Ratha-yatra;
[the Lord] told Advaita-chandra everything without reserve:
> "Nityananda and Advaita are not different, one form;
not understanding this, people speak of a quarrel.
> I entrust Nityananda to Advaita:
all the sacrifice of sankirtana is in your charge.
> Twenty-eight years* I have stayed in Nilachala;
I shall go to another place — I tell you without reserve.
> There will be many Vaishnavas and many Vaishnavis;
servants and servants of servants will fill the earth.
> The master of this house is Pandita Gosani;
there is no one dearer to me than he."
> Sri Haridasa Thakura stayed in Nilachala;
[the Lord] had a garden-retreat built for him by the sea.
> With many servants, in joy, Nityananda
Gaurachandra sent to the land of Gauda.
> In Ashadha Prataparudra sits in the Lord's house;
Advaita, smiling, speaks of Krishna.
> [p. 225]
> Standing, the Lord wets the string of his loincloth […];
"Give my body to the fire […], my life" […].*
> Mahendra Bharati died [by] […] haritaki;*
three hundred yatis put fire in his mouth.
> Haridasa Thakura departed first,
on the bright fourteenth day of Phalguna.
> In Ashadha, as he was dancing at the chariot procession,
suddenly a brick struck his left foot.
> Advaita set out at dawn for the land of Gauda;
in private [the Lord] told him something particular there.
> In the waters of Narendra, with all his companions,
Chaitanya sported in the water in many ways.
> On the sixth day the pain in his foot was great;
on that account he at last lay down in the Tota.
> To Pandita Gosani he told everything:
"Tomorrow, at the tenth danda of the night, I shall surely go."
> From somewhere came divine garlands of many colours;
how many vidyadharas dance on the royal road!
> "Bring the chariot, bring the chariot!" the gods call out;
the Lord mounted the chariot with the Garuda banner.
> The illusory body remained lying there;
Chaitanya went to Vaikuntha, leaving Jambudvipa.
> Many servants died of snakebite;
there were meteors, thunderbolts, earthquakes.
> Nityananda and Advaita Acharya Gosani heard;
Vishnupriya and Shachi Thakurani fainted.
> Sri Ramadasa [came] with all the companions;
Nityananda consoled [them], giving them comfort.
> Purushottama and the other companions of Advaita,
hearing of Chaitanya's departure, were struck dumb.
> In separation from Chaitanya, Nityananda constantly
listens to [the tale of] the lila of Chaitanya's departure.
> Nityananda, consoling all the companions,
dances in the bliss of Chaitanya, in the wealth of kirtana:
> "If I bear the name Nityananda Svarupa,
if I do not make Vaishnavas of all, down to the chandala, [—]
> I will make no distinction of caste for chandala or yavana;
giving prema-bhakti to all, I will make them dance in kirtana."
> Sri Ramadasa holds all power:
he will reveal the fifty-six crores of the Yadu line.
> "I will make the wives of good families dance in the bliss of kirtana;
the blind, the deaf and the dull will dance at will.
> I will bring Chaitanya, I will make people accept that Chaitanya;
I will make the kingdoms of Gauda and Utkala blessed, blessed."
> Hearing this vow of Nityananda,
all the Vaishnavas raise the cry, "Glory, glory!"
> After some days Nityananda, wearing the shikha and the sacred thread,
wandered the earth in the guise of a great wrestler.
> The daughters of Suryadasa, Sri Vasu and Jahnava,*
he took in marriage, freely and merrily.
> From Vasu's womb appeared Gosani Virabhadra;
Jahnava's son is Ramabhadra, a great wrestler.*
> Murari Chaitanyadasa catches and brings a tiger;
he sleeps on a bed of snakes — all people know it.
> Sri Sundarananda Thakura, in the water,
catches a crocodile and brings it before everyone.
> Disputing with the Kazi, in the madness of prema,
Gangadasa stayed seven days in a pool of the Ganga.
> Great was the madness of prema of Kamalakara Pippalai:
he cut his own body, and yet he did not come to himself.
> Gadadhara Dasa disputed with the Kazi
and leapt into a pit of fire — seeing it, the people were afraid.
> Purushottama Dasa ate the poison of the mandara*
and digested the poison by the power of the bliss of prema.
> [p. 226]
> As Sanjaya Pandita danced in the mood of a child,
suddenly a snake came out of his mouth.
> In ecstasy Murari Gupta became Hanuman:
a tail came out of him, twelve cubits long.
> Purandara Pandita climbs to the top of a tree;
a sixteen-cubit tail hangs down to the foot of the tree.
> Parameshvara Dasa ate three measures* of earth;
Balarama Dasa burns [the dwellings?] of the yavanas.*
> Kaliya Krishnadasa binds and brings a crocodile;
seeing it, Sri Nityananda's delight increased.
> Sri Nityananda made his home at Khardaha,
where the line of the great kulina Yogeshvara lives.*
> Advaita-chandra's line dwells in Shantipur:
the sons and grandsons of Sita and Advaita appear.
> Sankirtana and temples will be in every kingdom:
[by this] weighty deed he removed the earth's burden.
> The treasure of Chaitanya's life is Lord Nityananda:
not for an instant did he see [him] in separation, as if he were blind.*
> Nityananda always stays at home;
Gauridasa Pandita gives him help.
> Gauridasa Pandita — the four brothers together —
with Nityananda merrily carry on the dhamali of rapture.
> Thousands upon thousands — so many servants of Advaita!
Their servants fill the world.
> The servants of Chaitanya are without limit;
the servants of Nityananda have great prosperity.
> All the servants who are with Nityananda-chandra
I could not tell in a thousand years.
> Each servant has a following of thousands upon thousands;
by Nityananda's grace they are like Krishna.
> In the Kali age the world became righteous;
all the heavy burden of the earth was removed.
> Nityananda said to Gauridasa Pandita:
"[…] Pandita, I remain on this earth."*
> In the month of Ashvina, at a conjunction, on the dark eighth lunar day,
Nityananda went to Vaikuntha, leaving the earth.
> On the day of Ekadashi it was like the dissolution of the world:
at the breath of Ananta the earth trembled.
> The mahantas who heard of Nityananda's departure,
seeing Virabhadra, were wholly comforted.
> Sita and Advaita were left with great grief in their hearts:
"Alas, Chaitanya, Nityananda Svarupa!"
> Acharya Gosani passed some more days;
"I shall leave the earth," he said of his own accord.
> On the bright thirteenth lunar day of the month of Pausha
Acharya Gosani departed to Vaikuntha.
> Svasti! Glory, glory to the Chaitanya-mangala,
the crest-jewel of avataras, in which all is revealed!
> Whoever sings of Chaitanya, or makes others sing of Chaitanya,
is Chaitanya's servant, and Chaitanya is his helper.
> To his sons, grandsons, great-grandsons and all the rest
Jayananda's blessing: the fulfilment of their wishes.
> Meditating on the two feet of Chaitanya and Gadadhara,
Jayananda joyfully sings the Uttara-khanda." The end.
notes: "রুধিআ মাএর মুখে ইটাল মারিঞা" — the sense is conjectural.
Hari-vasara — the Ekadashi day; the episode meant is the one in which the child Nimai demanded and ate the food prepared as an offering to Vishnu in the house of Jagadisha and Hiranya.
"চৈতন্যেতে গুরুতে মারিল পুথির বাড়ি" — the beginning of the line is unclear.
"ছালিয়াধরা" — the name (or nickname) is unidentified; the reading follows the OCR.
"পাটুআ" — jute (or jute leaves eaten as a vegetable); Sridhara is the poor trader with whom, according to the biographies, Nimai bargained in the market.
"সাপে মুক্ত করিল কুকুর গঙ্গাদাস" — the sense is unclear (taken as "শাপে মুক্ত," "freed from a curse").
"পণ্ডিত হএ বক," literally "panditas become herons," i.e. apparently they fall dumb or look foolish; the sense is conjectural.
A digvijayi, "conqueror of the quarters," is a wandering scholar who defeated all comers in debate.
I.e. Lakshmipriya, Chaitanya's first wife.
"বাপ মরিতে গয়া যাইতে" — the journey to Gaya for the funeral rite for his father; Rajagiri (Rajgir) — hills near Gaya.
The connection of the line with its context is unclear: Madhavendra Puri was the guru of Ishvara Puri.
"বুড়ি," an old woman; the episode is known only from Jayananda.
"বায়ু," "wind," i.e. a disorder of the wind (vata) in the body — an illness taken for madness.
"বিষ্ণুখট্টা," the seat (couch) of Vishnu, i.e. the throne of the deity.
"দাসী-পুত্র," "son of a maidservant"; who is meant is unclear (perhaps Murari himself, so naming himself in humility).
The second line of this couplet is missing in the OCR.
"ধুবালিআ সিন্ধালিআ" — apparently nicknames of Jagai and Madhai; the reading follows the OCR.
The OCR has "নিশ্বলিয়া," "লিমলিয়া"; according to the biographies, the Kazi's house stood at Simulia (সিমুলিয়া) near Navadvipa.
"সাত-প্রহরিয়া ভাব," the ecstasy of "seven watches," i.e. the great manifestation (mahaprakasha) that lasted twenty-one hours.
"ভক্ত করি সভার বহিল সাজি ধুতি" — the sense is unclear.
"দুখী দাসী" may also be taken as a name: Duhkhi was a maidservant in Srivasa's house.
Whom the king's man seized is not clear from the text.
"আগম পুথি," the books of the agamas (tantras); perhaps Nityananda's abandonment of earlier rites is meant. The first line of the couplet is incomplete.
"উদ্‌গ্রাহ" — an argument or rejoinder in learned debate; cf. above, the section on language, word 9.
"ত্রিপাদ" — apparently the form of Trivikrama, who covered the worlds in three strides. The Kshetra is Puri.
"রদ্ক অনুগ্রহ মাত্র প্রদ্যুম্ন কানাঞি" — the line is corrupt (perhaps it concerns Pradyumna Mishra or Kanu).
Angada — one of the monkey leaders in the Ramayana.
"জম্বীর" — the lime (citron) tree.
Dana-khanda — songs about Krishna exacting "toll" from the gopis.
Dabir Khas and Sakar Malik — the court titles of Rupa and Sanatana in the service of the sultan of Gauda.
"দ্বার ছাড়ি" — perhaps Haridvar; the sense is conjectural.
Trimalla-raya — the deity on the Venkata hill (Tirumala, Venkateshvara); the second half of the line is unclear.
"কুড়িয়া গরুড়মিশ্র" — the reading follows the OCR; the person is unidentified.
Mahrat, Sorai, Viranchi — readings follow the OCR; the places are unidentified.
"হেমসেতু" — the sense is unclear (perhaps "as far as the Setu," i.e. the southern tip of India).

Vasu's note. According to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, [Chaitanya] lived twenty-four years as a householder and twenty-four years as a sannyasi in Nilachala. But according to Jayananda, Gauranga took sannyasa in his twentieth year, thus: "Fourth, the Sannyasa-khanda — listen with one mind — how [he took] sannyasa and the name Sri Krishna-Chaitanya. Young in years was Gaurachandra, twenty years old; a man of great renunciation, his body pure gold."
The couplet is corrupt ("দাঁড়াএ প্রভুর তিতে কৌপীনের ডোর। অগ্নি দেহ অন্য কনাএ কুঞ্জ প্রাণ মোর"); the rendering is a guess.
"হরিতকী কাষ্ঠে" — the sense is unclear; Mahendra Bharati is unidentified.
The OCR has "শ্রীবস্থ জানকী"; below it has "জাহ্নবীনন্দন," so we read "Jahnava." These are Vasudha and Jahnava, Nityananda's wives.
"জাহ্নবীনন্দন রামভদ্র মহামল্ল" — so in the text; cf. what is known of Ramachandra, Jahnava's adopted son.
"মণ্ডর বিষ" — reading and sense unclear.
"আড়ি" — a measure of grain.
"জবনের সাড়ি" — the sense is unclear.
I.e. the line to which Suryadasa, Nityananda's father-in-law, belonged.
The line is unclear; perhaps "like a blind man [without his guide]."
"নিষ্কপটে পণ্ডিত আমি আছি এই মহী" — the sense is unclear.

verses_en.text:
Nityananda consoled the disciples and vowed before them, "We will keep the Name alive. We will make all men down to the Chandals, Vaishnavs. We will not differentiate [low] castes like the Chandals or Muslims, but will give them all love and bhakti and make them all dance [with us] at kirtan. We will make the realms of Bengal and Orissa blessed." The Vaishnavs shouted applause at his words.
*: The first paragraph comes from the introductory part of the book, where Sarkar characterizes his sources; the rest is his translation at the end of the book. Sarkar's text is reproduced verbatim (spelling, punctuation and his square-bracketed additions kept; only line breaks and italics markup adapted). Translator's notes are added for the project.
*: Sarkar translates from the 1905 edition of the Chaitanya-mangala (Bangiya Sahitya Parishat, ed. N. Vasu and K. Nath). The same episode from Vasu's manuscript (folios 75–76) is translated in `02-vasu-1897.md` (the section on Mahaprabhu's disappearance, notes 67–68). Agreements: the wound from a brick to the left foot while dancing at the car festival; the secret word to Advaita before his departure for Gauda; the water-play in the Narendra lake; the pain growing worse on the sixth day; the Lord taking to his bed at Tota (Sarkar's "garden" is a literal rendering of tota); the words to the Pandita Gosani (probably Gadadhara) that he would depart the next night; the garlands, the dancing vidyadharas, the gods' cry "Bring the chariot!", the chariot with the Garuda banner (Sarkar: "figure … on its spire"); the body left on earth; the servants' death by snake-bite; the falling meteors and thunderbolts. Differences: Vasu's extract opens with two couplets absent in Sarkar (Chaitanya at Tota announces his departure and asks for the chariot to be sent on the bright seventh lunar day of Ashadha), and it ends with the portents, whereas Sarkar continues (the swoons of Nityananda, Advaita, Vishnupriya and Shachi, Purushottama's speechlessness, Nityananda's vow) beyond Vasu's quotation; Vasu's portents also include an earthquake, which Sarkar lacks; "the tenth danda of the night" (about four hours after sunset) is rendered by Sarkar as "10 o clock"; where Vasu has the "illusory body", Sarkar has the "material body"; the obscure word before "car procession" (Vasu, note 67) is passed over by Sarkar, who keeps only "Bijaya" (going forth, procession). Sarkar translates in free prose and abridges in places. Sarkar's dating (the poem c. 1568) is later than Vasu's (shortly after 1480 Shaka, i.e. c. 1558); the birth year c. 1511 agrees with Vasu's conclusions (`02-vasu-1897.md`, note 24).
